Then I define the spine chain itself off the hips joint with three segments, naming them spine1 through spine3 along a catmull path through several knots.

Then I'm setting up the head joint with a forward-leaning aim since the troll's neck is short and thick, positioning the head base slightly forward and up from the neck base, and defining the head's local axes using word-based directions (left/right/forward) to keep orientation unambiguous relative to the model's frame.

Now I'm moving into the actual head sculpting for the Warcraft troll: long face, heavy brow, massive lower jaw with upward tusks, swept-back pointed ears, drooping flat nose, and a mohawk, starting with a skull sphere positioned slightly forward and up from the head joint.

For the brow I'm shaping two angled slabs across the forehead to give that heavy, angry ridge look, tilting each one inward so the inner edges sit lower for a fierce expression.

For the eyes, I'm picturing small glowing amber troll-eyes nestled under that brow, likely using a plane with a texture for the glow effect.

I'm trusting that rotation and tweaking the y-angle slightly so each eye faces a bit outward instead of straight forward, adjusting by about 15 degrees from the base -90 orientation depending on which side the eye sits.

Recomputing confirms θ = -90+φ works with φ = s*20 for the left eye offset. I'll let the ring hang flat threading through the lower edge of the ear plate and not fuss further over orientation.

Writing blade geometry...

Still defining crest geometry...
